newsitem.title: UK: Eurobond issuers and investors get ready to pounce.
newsitem.headline: Eurobond issuers and investors get ready to pounce.

text.p: Borrowers are ready to raise funds in the Eurobond market and investors are eager to put their money to work next week after release of U.S. jobs data on Friday, syndicate officials in London said.
While uncertainty lingered about the interest rate outlook in the U.S. after the data, some said the Eurobond market would still need to get back to business after its recent lull.

"A build up of cash after two weeks of inactivity in the Eurobond market is burning a hole in investors' pockets and should be put to work next week if the underlying bond markets stabilise," a syndicate official at a U.S. bank said.
"The moment this market stabilises we'll see issuance resume."

March non-farm payrolls rose 175,000, down from 339,000 new jobs in February. But offsetting what was viewed as a debt market "friendly figure" was the rise in the hourly earnings up 4.0 percent, the highest since year ended June 1990.

The Eurobond market has hibernated for a fortnight ahead of the U.S. jobs data amid interest rate uncertainty. Some dealers expect another 25 basis point rise after the May 20 Federal Open Market Committee meeting.
Other syndicate officials are negative and suggest another lacklustre period next week, with only top credits able to tap funds.
"The high quality names will work, but interest rate uncertainty still remains and if the market is not good next week, it's going to hurt the issuers," a dealer said.
They said borrowers could shorten maturities to five years in anticipation of another U.S. interest rate rise. German banks are said to be eyeing the five-year sector.

Triple A-rated borrowers such as the Asian Development Bank and Fannie Mae are mooted to be eyeing the 10-year dollar sector. The European Investment Bank and World Bank are also eyeing opportunities, new issues dealers said.
"If we continue to see a sell-off in Treasuries we're going to see a hold off until the market stabilises," a new issues dealer said.
"But we cannot wait until May 20, we need to do business and as soon as we see a floor, we'll pounce."
